ownership_reason: Only the gold cuts the source path into names: hops 1 and 2 hold the command line and its options, hop 3 joins the source names into the path (each name after the first preceded by the path separator, per its javadoc, so a path of one name has no separator), hop 4 passes the path on with the source directory, and the gold returns one File per name. On the path 'tzdata' the gold's own name step cuts the name before a separator that the path does not hold (substring(0, -1)) and throws, although its javadoc promises the files named on the path and that path names one file. No hop can avoid it while keeping the documented path form: a separator added after the last name or before the first adds an empty name, which the gold resolves to the source directory itself, so compile fails reading a directory; answering the one-name path above the gold means resolving the name a second time outside the method that cuts paths into names. The convention that a delimited text without its delimiter is one whole item, handled by its own step, is pinned outside the gold: the facade's usage (<source files>: one or more names); ZoneInfoCompiler.parseDataFile cuts a line at '#' only when it holds one, so a line without a comment is read whole (TestDateTimeZone testForID_String_old and testGetID read zones compiled from such lines); ZoneInfoCompiler.Rule.formatName splits a 'GMT/BST' format only when it holds the '/' (TestDateTimeZone testGetNameKey: BST in summer, GMT in winter for Europe/London) and returns a format without the '%s' marker as it is, by its own early return.
